story.title: Story 1: Pull and Status on the Record

result.planSummary: Fixed SV-01-PULL-STATUS-001 at the seam layer: the verified side-effect path was openThreadDatabase → fireThreadTouch → scheduler.touch, which in a background SDK can hang a first-touch catch-up drain (queue claims, provider calls, writes) off a thread-view read. The fix is a reads-only operation scope in shared/context.ts — runWithThreadTouchSuppressed runs a function under the current instance seam with the touch announcement replaced by a no-op while preserving the poke target and view config (and delegating to the below-SDK defaults when no seam is in scope, minus the touch). thread-view pull and status wrap their entire bodies in this scope, which structurally covers not just their own openThreadDatabase calls but also the owners' report surfaces status consumes — no test-only bypass, no signature changes to the frozen messages/turns domains, and write paths are untouched so first-touch catch-up still works everywhere it should. A new background-mode test leg extends TC-1.2/TC-2.5: pending work is manufactured through a manual SDK, then a fresh background SDK pulls twice and reads status; it asserts work rows / form states / view rows / boundary unchanged (full below-SDK state snapshot), provider fake at zero calls, repeated pulls byte-identical via full-result hash, repeated status byte-identical, and pending work visible through the read itself — after settling the scheduler (timeout + drainSettled) so a wrongly-scheduled drain would surface. The regression test was proven live: with the suppression temporarily removed it fails (the catch-up drain fires), with the fix it passes.

changedFiles.reason: New runWithThreadTouchSuppressed: reads-only operation scope that suppresses the DD-10 open announcement under the current seam (poke and view config carried through; below-SDK fallback preserved minus touch)
pull and status bodies run inside the touch-suppressed scope so AC-1.1/AC-2.8 reads-only holds structurally in both host modes, covering their own opens and status's report-surface opens
New background-leg describe extending TC-1.2/TC-2.5: background SDK with pending work — no catch-up drain, state snapshot unchanged, zero provider calls, byte-identical repeated pulls and status
Re-recorded view-pull.test.ts hash after the verifier-mandated test addition (strengthening only; no existing assertion weakened)

added: test/view-pull.test.ts :: TC-1.2 / TC-2.5 background legs (SV-01-PULL-STATUS-001) :: schedules no catch-up drain: work rows, form states, provider count, and status all unchanged; repeated pulls byte-identical

findingsFixed: SV-01-PULL-STATUS-001: background-mode threadView.pull/status no longer fire the thread-touch announcement, so the scheduler's first-touch catch-up drain can never be scheduled by a read; verified by a regression test that fails when the suppression is removed and passes with it.
findingsSurfaced: The suppression is scoped to the thread-view ops, not to openThreadDatabase generally: other read surfaces (messages.listMessages, reports called directly) still announce opens, preserving Epic 02's first-touch catch-up behavior — only the Epic 03 reads carry the reads-only contract. If a later story wants all reads touch-free, the same scope function is the seam to apply.

openThreadDatabase still runs schema migrations on a pre-current-version file during pull/status (existing every-operation contract from Epic 01); the finding's queue/provider/write classes are closed, but a first open of a legacy file remains a schema write by design.
test/view-pull.test.ts was modified after its Red-manifest recording solely to ADD the verifier-mandated background legs; the manifest hash was re-recorded and no existing assertion was weakened.

result.recommendedNextStep: Re-run story verification for SV-01-PULL-STATUS-001 closure; Story 2 (compact) can proceed on the unchanged array-shape contract.
